title: Surgery- and Adjuvant Therapy-Related Decision Regret Following Microvascular Free Flap Reconstruction for Head and Neck Tumors: Associations with Fear of Disease Progression, Dysphagia, and Psychological Distress
summary:
We are investigating how people who have had oral or throat cancer feel about their treatment today. All participants had their tumors removed, and the operated area was reconstructed using their own tissue from another part of the body. They subsequently received radiation therapy.

Six months to five years after the end of treatment, the participants complete a one-time questionnaire. We are comparing whether and to what extent they regret their decisions to undergo surgery and radiation therapy in retrospect. Those who also received anticancer medications are asked about that as well. In addition, we are investigating whether this regret is related to difficulty swallowing, psychological distress, fear of the cancer returning, or quality of life.
conditions: Decision regret after curative treatment for squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, oropharynx, or hypopharynx
Malignant neoplasms of lip, oral cavity and pharynx

interventions.name: Adults with squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, oropharynx, or hypopharynx who have undergone curative resection with microvascular free flap reconstruction and adjuvant radiation therapy or chemoradiation therapy, at least 6 months after the end of treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histologically confirmed squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity, oropharynx, or hypopharynx

Curative-intent tumor resection with microvascular free flap reconstruction

Completion of adjuvant radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy 6 to 60 months before enrollment

No evidence of active recurrence or distant metastases at the time of the survey

Ability to understand and complete questionnaires in German

Written or electronic informed consent to study participation and data processing
Exclusion criteria:
Palliative intent of the initial treatment

Active local or regional recurrence or distant metastases at the time of the survey

Salvage surgery after definitive chemoradiotherapy

Initial surgery followed by definitive chemoradiotherapy for recurrent disease

Second malignancy associated with a substantial current treatment burden

Laryngeal carcinoma

Severe cognitive impairment, insufficient German language proficiency, or inability to provide informed consent
